raw:
The dueling schedule is posted on a slate board beside the octagon, its white lettering refreshed by a hovering lamp-globe.

**Eleventh bell — Ranked bout, first tier:** Ashara vel Kothren vs. Tovan Rimeclaw.

You have time.

By the eleventh bell, a loose crowd has gathered along the low rail around the packed-earth octagon. The storm lies far below the terrace, turning the sky beneath the plateau a bruised silver. Ashara waits inside the ring in padded black practice armor, her tied hair damp at the temples and a blunted sword balanced loosely in one hand.

Her opponent is broad-shouldered and furred along the jaw and forearms, wearing blue wraps over one elbow. He gives Ashara a polite nod before taking his guard.

Rashid stands near the rail, arms folded. He notices you arrive but keeps his attention on the ring.

The signal sounds.

Tovan opens hard, trying to drive her backward with his size. Ashara gives him ground for three steps, then changes the angle so abruptly that his next strike meets empty space. Her practice blade raps his ribs. Once. Twice.

The crowd makes the small approving noise of people who recognize clean work.

Tovan adjusts, more cautious now. He catches her next attack, forces her blade low, and nearly lands a touch at her shoulder. Ashara twists away; her tail lashes for balance, and she comes back inside his reach before he can reset. The flat of her blade strikes his wrist. His weapon falls into the dirt.

The second signal ends it.

Tovan retrieves his sword and bows with visible annoyance, though he says something that makes Ashara’s mouth briefly curve. The ranking clerk marks the result beside the slate: **Kothren retains first tier.**

Rashid exhales through his nose. “Her third exchange was better than yesterday.”

Ashara steps out of the octagon, accepts a towel from an attendant, and catches sight of you among the spectators. Her gaze rests there for a moment before she turns back to the clerk to sign the result.
